newsitem.title: USA: One killed, one hurt in Penn State campus shooting.
newsitem.headline: One killed, one hurt in Penn State campus shooting.

text.p: A student was killed and another critically wounded on Tuesday morning when a woman opened fire with a high-powered rifle at Pennsylvania State University campus, officials said.
The attacker, identified as Jillian Robbins, 19, was disarmed by another student who wrestled the seven millimetre Mauser rifle from her after she had fired five shots.
She was quickly apprehended by university police.
Robbins was not a university student but lived in a nearby community, university spokeswoman Kathy Norris said.
"She fired five shots," Norris said. "She said she saw two people go down."
Melanie Ann Spalla, a 19-year-old communications student, was killed and another student, Nicholas Mensah, 27, was critically injured in the shooting, officials said.
The fatal shooting occurred outside the university's student centre building and shocked the campus community.
University police officers said Robbins gave no reason for the shooting and said she did not know anyone involved.
Police said Brendon Malovrh, an undergraduate student, struggled with Robbins and wrestled the rifle from her hands. Robbins drew a knife, lunged at Malovrh and then stabbed herself in the leg.
Police found Malovrh, who was unhurt, applying a tourniquet to Robbins' leg when they arrived at the scene.
Mensah underwent surgery at Centre Community Hospital and was upgraded to stable condition by Tuesday afternoon. Robbins underwent surgery for the stab wound and was also listed in stable condition.
Eyewitnesses said they saw Robbins hiding under a tree near the student centre before firing the shots, police said.

Dave Stormer, assistant vice president for university safety, said background checks on Robbins had so far produced no criminal record. He said an arraignment would probably be held in a couple of days.
University President Graham B. Spanier called the incident "a random act of violence" and said in a news release that the campus was still a safe environment.
But students said they felt scared that such a violent act could occur on a rural campus in central Pennsylvania.
"It's scary to think someone can just walk onto campus and pick people off," said Jim Iovino, 20.
"These are things you hear about in big cities. Not here," another student said.
Iovino said he heard a shot while walking into a classroom and ignored it. "I thought it was just somebody lighting off firecrackers," he said.
But when he heard two more shots he looked out of a classroom window and saw Mensah lying on the ground, he said.
